title: Coefficient-stage vanishing for the smooth exceptional constant

from.place: Coefficient-stage geometric vanishing input used by the native comparison

statement: For a finite-field coefficient setting P, a separated finite-type model X₀, a normalized exceptional system S, and a smooth structure morphism of relative dimension d, there is a normalized comparison family C whose exceptional constant endpoint is zero in every homology degree other than -2d, and whose values identify the native Weil homology of every supplied exceptional adjunction with that endpoint.

source.place: Smooth specialization at the coefficient stage, followed by the normalized native coefficient comparison.

proof.text: Base change the structure morphism to the chosen geometric field; smoothness of relative dimension d is stable under base change. Apply RationalSmoothPurityCanonical.commonIso to the coefficient unit. The third equality of constant_purity_frobenius_square is precisely the intertwining equation for this isomorphism. Endofunctor.IsoAlgebra.isoMk therefore gives a proved isomorphism from twistedConstant P X0 d to exceptionalConstant P X0 c0 S. All geometric instances are those inherited from the fixed arithmetic model.

Obtain one normalized comparison family C with its native exceptional comparison and its all-degree shifted-Tate comparison from lem-sf-coefficient-shifted-tate-comparison. Preserve its first clause verbatim. For n not equal to -2d, WeilSheaf.isZero_homologySheaf_shift_toComplex computes the native cohomology of the shifted Tate sheaf tensor constant as zero; integer arithmetic identifies the excluded degree. Transport this zero object along the Tate comparison, then along C_n applied to the inverse of the proved smooth-purity pair isomorphism. This proves the desired exceptional endpoint vanishing for the same C in every degree.

proof_origin.place: Smooth specialization, with the Frobenius-pair isomorphism proved in Lean and shifted single-sheaf cohomology computed by the existing native homology-shift theorem.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_coefficient_exceptional_vanishing (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d X₀.hom] : ∃ C : ℤ → (Pairs P X₀ ⥤ WeilSheaf P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left), (∀ (J : WeilComplex P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l (Spec (.of P.field.k₀)) ⥤ WeilComplex P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left) (adj : WeilComplex.derivedLowerShriek P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.hom ⊣ J) (n : ℤ), Nonempty ((WeilComplex.homologySheaf n).obj (J.obj (WeilSheaf.toComplex.obj (WeilSheaf.adicConstant P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l (Spec (.of P.field.k₀))))) ≅ (C n).obj (exceptionalConstant P X₀ c₀ S))) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, n ≠ -2 * (d : ℤ) → IsZero ((C n).obj (exceptionalConstant P X₀ c₀ S)))
